# infrawrench_jit_access_policy (Resource)

A just-in-time access policy: which **cloud roles** members may request on a connected account, for how long, who may ask, and who must approve. When a request under the policy is approved, the account's provider grants the role (an IAM Identity Center account assignment on AWS, a project IAM binding with a time-bound IAM Condition on Google Cloud, a RoleBinding on Kubernetes) and Infrawrench removes it when the window ends.

Requests and grants are runtime objects and are deliberately not resources: they are raised and decided by people, on a stated reason, and API keys cannot act on them at all. This resource manages only the policy, which API keys may write.

Not to be confused with break-glass access, which elevates Infrawrench permissions and never touches a cloud.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Production admin, on request: two hours at most, approved by whoever is on
# call (or the platform leads), and self-approvable only while a declared
# incident is open.
data "infrawrench_accounts" "aws" {
  plugin_id = "aws"
}

resource "infrawrench_jit_access_policy" "prod_admin" {
  name        = "Production admin for on-call"
  description = "Break-fix access to the production AWS account."
  account_id  = data.infrawrench_accounts.aws.accounts[0].id

  # An AWS account id and an IAM Identity Center permission set ARN. The
  # settings page offers both as pickers; copy them from there.
  target {
    scope_id   = "123456789012"
    scope_name = "production"
    role_id    = "arn:aws:sso:::permissionSet/ssoins-1111111111111111/ps-2222222222222222"
    role_name  = "AdministratorAccess"
  }

  max_duration_minutes     = 120
  default_duration_minutes = 60
  request_timeout_minutes  = 30

  approver_on_call_schedule_ids = [infrawrench_on_call_schedule.platform_primary.id]
  approver_role_ids             = ["role-platform-leads"]

  allow_self_approval_during_incident = true
  require_ticket                      = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `account_id` (String) Id of the connected account whose provider grants the roles (see the `infrawrench_accounts` data source). Its plugin must support just-in-time access: AWS (IAM Identity Center), Google Cloud or Kubernetes.
- `max_duration_minutes` (Number) Longest window a request may ask for, and the ceiling on the whole window after extensions, 5–720 minutes.
- `name` (String) What the policy is called, 1–120 characters, e.g. `Production admin for on-call`.

### Optional

- `allow_self_approval_during_incident` (Boolean) Let an approver approve their **own** request while a declared incident is open, for their own principal only. Recorded as self-approved, with the incident, in the request and the audit log.
- `approver_on_call_schedule_ids` (List of String) Ids of `infrawrench_on_call_schedule` rotations, up to 200; whoever is on call on one of them at decision time may approve.
- `approver_role_ids` (List of String) Team role ids whose members may approve, up to 200.
- `approver_user_ids` (List of String) Member ids who may approve, up to 200. The approver set is the union of the three approver lists, evaluated at decision time; at least one approver is required.
- `default_duration_minutes` (Number) Window the request form starts on, 5–720 minutes and no longer than `max_duration_minutes`. Defaults to 60 minutes or the maximum, whichever is shorter.
- `description` (String) Free text shown to requesters and approvers, up to 1000 characters.
- `enabled` (Boolean) A disabled policy accepts no new requests and has no approvers, so its pending requests time out. Grants it already made still end on time.
- `request_timeout_minutes` (Number) How long an undecided request stays decidable, 5–1440 minutes. No decision counts as a denial.
- `requester_role_ids` (List of String) Team role ids whose members may request, up to 200.
- `requester_user_ids` (List of String) Member ids who may request under this policy, up to 200. With `requester_role_ids` also empty, every member holding `access:request` may.
- `require_reason` (Boolean) Require a reason of at least 10 characters on every request.
- `require_ticket` (Boolean) Require a ticket or incident reference on every request.
- `target` (Block List) One scope and role pair members may request, 1–50 of them. The ids are the provider's own: an AWS account id and a permission set ARN, a GCP project id and a role name such as `roles/storage.admin`, or a Kubernetes namespace (or `*cluster*` for the whole cluster) and `ClusterRole:<name>` / `Role:<name>`. The settings page offers all of them as pickers. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--target))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Server-assigned policy id. Use it with `terraform import`.

<a id="nestedblock--target"></a>
### Nested Schema for `target`

Required:

- `role_id` (String) Provider id of the role, 1–1224 characters.
- `scope_id` (String) Provider id of the scope, 1–1224 characters.

Optional:

- `role_name` (String) Display name for the role, up to 300 characters. Omit it rather than repeating the id.
- `scope_name` (String) Display name for the scope, up to 300 characters. Omit it rather than repeating the id: the id is then shown.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# The id is in the --json output of `infrawrench jit policies`, and in the
# policy's row in Settings, Just-in-time Access.
terraform import infrawrench_jit_access_policy.prod_admin 6f1e2d3c-4b5a-4968-8776-5a4b3c2d1e0f
```
